request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Information:
Name: [Redacted]
Age: 53
Sex: Female
Date of admission: [Redacted]
Date of discharge: [Redacted]

Hospital Course:

The patient was admitted with a one-week history of abdominal pain, constipation, nausea, vomiting, and a single episode of bright red blood per rectum. Two days following her presentation, she developed bilateral facial weakness, perioral numbness, and difficulty in swallowing initiation. On examination, the patient had diminished bilateral facial musculature strength and an absent left patellar reflex. CT and MRI of the brain were obtained and showed changes consistent with chronic small vessel ischemic disease. Neurology was consulted and recommended a lumbar puncture which showed increased protein with absent white and red blood cells, raising the suspicion of Guillain-Barré syndrome. The patient was started on intravenous immunoglobulins and monitored in the progressive care unit. After a five-day course of IVIG, the patient showed a slight improvement but did not show up for her follow-up appointment and left against medical advice on day 9 of hospitalization.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Instructions:

The patient is advised to seek medical attention immediately if she experiences any new neurological symptoms such as numbness, tingling, or weakness in the extremities. She is also advised to attend all scheduled follow-up appointments and continue any prescribed medications as per the instructions of her primary care physician.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The principal diagnosis is Guillain-Barré syndrome (G61.0), so the category is **G61**.

- **Main reason for the stay:** She presented with abdominal pain, constipation, vomiting and a single episode of rectal bleeding. Within two days she developed bilateral facial weakness, perioral numbness, trouble starting a swallow and an absent left patellar reflex.
- **Investigations:** Lumbar puncture showed raised protein with no white cells. This pattern (albuminocytologic dissociation) supports Guillain-Barré syndrome. The facial diplegia pattern fits a Guillain-Barré variant. The brain imaging changes were chronic and incidental.
- **Treatment:** Most of the admission went to managing this condition. She had a five-day course of IVIG and monitoring in the progressive care unit.
- **Why not the abdominal symptoms:** They were the presenting complaint, but no separate gastrointestinal condition was established as the cause of the admission. They are best read as a preceding illness or part of the same process.
- **Chapter:** Guillain-Barré syndrome is a nervous system disorder, which gives chapter **G**.

CODE: G61
